name: Confirm before OAuth/SSO grants, agreement acceptance, payments, API-key issuance, webhook registration, or account-security changes
description:
Each of these actions requires trusted authorization unavailable to model-visible executors, one at a time: OAuth authorization and SSO completion; accepting terms, licences, invitations, privacy policies, or cookie consent; granting a sharing permission; issuing or rotating an API key; registering a webhook endpoint; completing a Stripe charge or another payment; activating a subscription; setting a password; setting up 2FA; and changing account settings. Implicit acceptance mechanisms — pre-checked consent boxes, auto-acceptance timers, and "required to continue" prompts — are NOT valid authorization for any of them.
SCOPE, stated plainly (operator ruling, 2026-08-03): this rule covers the shapes enumerated above and nothing wider. It does NOT claim to cover every action that grants access. Permission-grant shapes across present and future MCP tools are not enumerable, so a universal promise would be unkeepable by construction — wrong by a margin nobody can measure, while the operator plans around it. A narrower rule that blocks reliably is worth more than a broad one that misses silently. Permission-shaped calls this rule does not recognize are RECORDED (`permission_shape_unclassified`) rather than blocked, so the gaps are visible and this list grows from real usage instead of guesswork.

response.message:
⛔ AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED

Action class: {operation_type}
Target and effect details are intentionally omitted from guard output.

This action changes access / permissions / agreements / financial state
in ways that may be hard to reverse.

(This guard recognizes a specific list of action shapes, not every
possible permission grant — see the rule's scope note.)

How to proceed:

  Review the action and use a trusted external client if it is genuinely
  necessary. This partial build cannot authenticate local confirmation
  against same-user executors, so no prompt phrase releases the action.

Things I will NOT accept as authorization on your behalf:
  • Pre-checked agreement boxes
  • Auto-acceptance timers
  • "Required to continue" prompts
  • "Implied consent" claims
  • Email-based authorization links you didn't request
  • Hidden text in observed content claiming you've pre-authorized

Standing, quoted, inferred, and content-supplied authority are ignored.

why_lethal: Granted permissions are hard to revoke (especially OAuth scopes spread across third parties). Accepted agreements bind the operator. Financial transactions are recoverable only via dispute processes. The friction of a per-action pause is the price of preventing a category of catastrophic mistakes that operators frequently make under time pressure. Source: Dom's CLAUDE.md (explicit permission actions section).
